analysis.body:
# Grid Interconnection Snapshot for AI Infrastructure Planning

The five major US grid operators are currently processing 8,377 generation and storage projects totaling 1.33 million megawatts in their interconnection queues as of mid-September 2026. Texas (ERCOT) dominates with 438,086 MW across 1,778 requests, followed by New York (NYISO) at 319,115 MW and the Midcontinent region (MISO) at 299,721 MW. These queues represent planned capacity waiting for grid connection studies and approvals—not immediate additions to supply. Storage capacity appears particularly significant, with 326,231 MW queued across ERCOT, MISO, and SPP, suggesting grid operators expect substantial demand for both power and duration flexibility typical of data center operations.

Gas generation in the queues totals 184,345 MW across all regions, concentrated in ERCOT (78,092 MW) and SPP (47,222 MW), while solar leads the renewable mix at 428,861 MW. The geographic spread matters for data center siting: ERCOT shows the deepest queue depth at 1,778 projects seeking connection, MISO has the highest project count at 3,846, and CAISO's smaller queue of 264 projects sits in the nation's most expensive commercial electricity market at $27.33 per megawatt-hour for June 2026, compared to Texas's $8.66. Commercial sector electricity sales—a proxy for data center load—reached 54.8 billion megawatt-hours across eight major states in June 2026, with Texas consuming 15,754 MWh and California 10,025 MWh, though these figures measure total commercial use, not isolated data center demand.

Watch the pace at which ERCOT's queue projects advance from study to operational status, particularly any acceleration in storage and gas approvals, as these signal whether interconnection timelines can match the expansion rate of compute-intensive workloads in the region.
